arxiv-2110-01332.title: Moore-Penrose inverse and applications to linear equations
arxiv-2110-01332.creator: Y. Estaremi and S. Shamsi
arxiv-2110-01332.description: Abstract . In the present paper we investigate Moore-Penrose inverse and characteristic matrix of unbounded WCT operators on the Hilbert space L 2 ​ ( μ ) L^{2}(\mu) . Also, we obtain some applications of the Moore-Penrose inverse of unbounded operators on the Hilbert space ℋ \mathcal{H} to variational regularization problem.

arxiv-2302-10153.title: Global torus blocks in the necklace channel
arxiv-2302-10153.creator: Mikhail Pavlov
arxiv-2302-10153.description: Abstract We continue studying of global conformal blocks on the torus in a special (necklace) channel. Functions of such multi-point blocks are explicitly found under special conditions on the blocks’ conformal dimensions. We have verified that these blocks satisfy the Casimir equations, which were derived in previous studies.

arxiv-2307-12293.title: Dissipative learning of a quantum classifier
arxiv-2307-12293.creator: Ufuk Korkmaz, Deniz Türkpençe
arxiv-2307-12293.description: Abstract The expectation that quantum computation might bring performance advantages in machine learning algorithms motivates the work on the quantum versions of artificial neural networks. In this study, we analyze the learning dynamics of a quantum classifier model that works as an open quantum system which is an alternative to the standard quantum circuit model.

arxiv-2502-13082.title: Automated Linear Parameter-Varying Modeling of Nonlinear Systems: A Global Embedding Approach footnoteinfo This research was supported by the European Space Agency (grant number: 4000145530) and The MathWorks Inc. Opinions, findings, conclusions or recommendations expressed in this abstract are thos
arxiv-2502-13082.creator: E. Javier Olucha, Patrick J. W. Koelewijn, Amritam Das, Roland Tóth
arxiv-2502-13082.description: Abstract In this paper, an automated linear parameter-varying (LPV) model conversion approach is proposed for nonlinear dynamical systems. The proposed method achieves global embedding of the original nonlinear behavior of the system by leveraging the second fundamental theorem of calculus to factorize matrix function expressions without any approximation.

arxiv-2510-14284.title: Stability and Heavy-traffic Delay Optimality of General Load Balancing Policies in Heterogeneous Service Systems
arxiv-2510-14284.creator: Yishun Luolabel=e2]luo00329@umn.edu, Martin Zubeldialabel=e1]zubeldia@umn.edu
arxiv-2510-14284.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Yishun Luolabel=e2]luo00329@umn.edu, Martin Zubeldialabel=e1]zubeldia@umn.edu. We consider a load balancing system consisting of n n single-server queues working in parallel, with heterogeneous service rates. Jobs arrive to a central dispatcher, which has to dispatch them to one of the queues immediately upon arrival. For this setting, we consider a broad family of policies where the dispatcher can only access the queue lengths sporadically, every T T units of time.

arxiv-2510-26645.title: Curly Flow Matching for Learning Non-gradient Field Dynamics
arxiv-2510-26645.creator: Katarina Petrović, Lazar Atanackovic, Viggo Moro, Kacper Kapuśniak, İsmail İlkan Ceylan, Michael Bronstein, Avishek Joey Bose, Alexander Tong
arxiv-2510-26645.description: Abstract Modeling the transport dynamics of natural processes from population-level observations is a ubiquitous problem in the natural sciences. Such models rely on key assumptions about the underlying process in order to enable faithful learning of governing dynamics that mimic the actual system behavior.

govdocs-nsarchive-Briefing_Book_nuclear-.creator: National Security Archive
govdocs-nsarchive-Briefing_Book_nuclear-.description: Reflecting the Cold War tensions of the time, the briefing outline, originally classified Top Secret, posited possible Soviet acts of aggression, “what the Russians could do to us,” with a possible conflict escalating to nuclear strikes on the United States. According to the briefing, without civil defense a massive Soviet attack could kill 80 million Americans.

pmc-10507317.title: Population pharmacokinetics of Amisulpride in Chinese patients with schizophrenia with external validation: the impact of renal function
pmc-10507317.creator: Anning Li, Wen Yao Mak, Tingyi Ruan, Fang Dong, Nan Zheng, Meng Gu, Wei Guo, Jingye Zhang, Haoxuan Cheng, Canjun Ruan, Yufei Shi, Yannan Zang, Xuequan Zhu, Qingfeng He, Xiaoqiang Xiang, Gang Wang, Xiao Zhu
pmc-10507317.description: Introduction: Amisulpride is primarily eliminated via the kidneys. Given the clear influence of renal clearance on plasma concentration, we aimed to explicitly examine the impact of renal function on amisulpride pharmacokinetics (PK) via population PK modelling and Monte Carlo simulations. Method: Plasma concentrations from 921 patients (776 in development and 145 in validation) were utilized.

pmc-10653065.title: Preparation and Characterization of Extruded PLA Films Coated with Polyaniline or Polypyrrole by In Situ Chemical Polymerization
pmc-10653065.creator: José
pmc-10653065.description: Conductive polymers, such as polypyrrole and polyaniline, have been extensively studied for their notable intrinsic electronic and ionic conductivities, rendering them suitable for a range of diverse applications. In this study, in situ chemical polymerization was employed to coat extruded PLA films with PPy and PANi.

pmc-11599580.title: The role of the social network in the study of adherence to diabetic retinopathy screening programs
pmc-11599580.creator: Andreia Penso Pereira, Ana Afonso, Raul M. S. Laureano, Fernando Buarque de Lima Neto
pmc-11599580.description: Diabetic retinopathy screenings are a vital strategy to avoid the severe consequences of this disease. However, their success depends on the adherence of the target population. The present work aims to review the adherence to diabetic retinopathy screening, more specifically the influence of the persons with diabetes’ social network (contacts between persons with diabetes) on their screening behaviour.

pmc-11610490.title: Advances in the use of metal-free tetrapyrrolic macrocycles as catalysts
pmc-11610490.creator: Mandeep K Chahal, Joseph W Meisel, Amar H Flood
pmc-11610490.description: This review provides an overview of recent progress made in the field of catalysis using metal-free tetrapyrrolic macrocycles, focusing on calix[4]pyrroles, porphyrins and corroles, which are structurally related to porphyrins. Calix[4]pyrroles are versatile receptors in supramolecular chemistry while porphyrins are considered as ‘pigment of life’ due to their role in vital biological processes.

pmc-11616302.title: Genomic and clinical characterization of pediatric lymphoepithelioma-like carcinoma
pmc-11616302.creator: Yi Que, Xiuxia Lu, Suying Lu, Feifei Sun, Jia Zhu, Yu Zhang, Juan Wang, Junting Huang, Wei Liu, Fenghua Wang, Liping Li, Li Zhang, Min Gao, Zijun Zhen, Yizhuo Zhang
pmc-11616302.description: BackgroundPediatric lymphoepithelioma-like carcinoma (pLELC) is a rare neoplasm with unclear prognosis, genome, and tumor microenvironment. Our study aims to elucidate its genomic and clinical characteristics.MethodsForty-one pLELC patients were enrolled at Sun Yat-sen University Cancer Center from 2012 to 2023. Kaplan–Meier analysis was utilized to estimate progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS).

pmc-12118258.title: Pediatric postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome: From mechanisms to individualized management
pmc-12118258.creator: Wenrui Xu, Hongfang Jin, Ying Liao, Junbao Du
pmc-12118258.description: Postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome (POTS) represents chronic orthostatic intolerance. Patients usually suffer from presyncopal symptoms, such as lightheadedness, headache, blurred vision, and fatigue. Central hypovolemia, peripheral vascular dysfunction, and a hyperadrenergic state may contribute to the pathogenesis of POTS. It is necessary to comprehensively assess the clinical characteristics, physiological changes, and biochemical markers to select an appropriate therapy.

pmc-12358546.title: Characterization of nanoplastics and small-sized microplastics in sewage treatment
pmc-12358546.creator: Shaima Iskandarani, Sarvajith Manjunath, Rosa Busquets, Lorenzo Raeli, Pascal E Saikaly, Luiza C Campos
pmc-12358546.description: The presence of nanoplastics (NPs) in sewage treatment plants (STPs) remains a critical yet underexplored environmental issue. Here, we present a novel investigation into the occurrence, recovery, and characterization of nanoplastics and small-size microplastics (50–2500 nm) in raw and treated sewage effluent from a full-scale STP (treating 4000 m3/day) operating with activated sludge.

pmc-12522772.title: Determinants of malaria transmission in Indian districts in 2018: insights from ensemble models
pmc-12522772.creator: Avik Kumar Sam, Alisha Khatoon, Harish C. Phuleria
pmc-12522772.description: BackgroundThe National Framework for Malaria Elimination, formulated in 2016, aims to eliminate malaria in India by 2030, focusing on the districts as the strategic units for planning and implementing intervention measures. In this study, the spatial distribution of malaria hotspots was investigated and the significant covariates were identified that are potentially influencing its transmission in India.

pmc-12564550.title: Narciclasine as a Novel Treatment for Lung Cancer and Malignant Pleural Mesothelioma: Insights from 3D Tumor Spheroid Models
pmc-12564550.creator: Sicong Jiang, Serkan Berkcan, Nadja Perriraz-Mayer, Frédéric Triponez, Véronique Serre-Beinier, Qibiao Wu, Hiu Yee Kwan
pmc-12564550.description: Thoracic tumors, including lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) and malignant pleural mesothelioma (MM), remain a leading cause of cancer-related deaths, primarily due to the challenges in treating advanced thoracic tumors. New drugs with optimal efficacy and minimal side effects are required. Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) compounds offer a promising alternative.

pmc-12569676.title: Long-Range Interaction between Molecules with Electronic Degeneracy: Beyond the Born–Oppenheimer Approximation
pmc-12569676.creator: Yipeng Yu, Xixi Hu, Hua Guo, Daiqian Xie
pmc-12569676.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Long-range intermolecular interaction plays an essential role in (ultra)­cold collisions. For monomers with degenerate electronic states, an accurate description of the long-range interaction can be challenging due to the potential breakdown of the Born–Oppenheimer approximation. In this work, we developed a general method to construct long-range interaction potential energy surfaces (IPESs) between arbitrary molecules using the degenerate perturbation theory of Schrödinger.

pmc-12587672.title: ‘How nice would it be!’: synergies between pro-choice female physicians and abortion acompañantes in Mexico
pmc-12587672.creator: Suzanne Veldhuis, Georgina Sánchez Ramírez, Maribel Campos Muñuzuri, Blair G. Darney
pmc-12587672.description: BackgroundPro-choice female physicians and abortion acompañantes– feminist activists who provide information and accompaniment during self-managed medication abortions– each contribute to safe abortion access in Mexico. Synergistic collaboration between these actors could improve access to safe and high-quality abortion care. We explored the possibility of synergy between pro-choice female physicians and acompañantes in Mexico.MethodsThis qualitative research is based on feminist epistemology.

pmc-13526809.title: Diagnostic efficacy of circulating tumor cell in clinically significant prostate cancer
pmc-13526809.creator: Jiajun Qian, Fan Zhao, Bo Cai, Yangbo Guan, Huyang Xie, Xiang Zhang, Limin Ma
pmc-13526809.description: To investigate the value of circulating tumor cells (CTC) in the diagnosis of clinically significant prostate cancer (csPCa). Patients who underwent prostate biopsy under ultrasound guidance and CTC detection at Nantong University Affiliated Hospital from December 2023 to June 2024 were included. Based on the CTC detection results, patients were divided into CTC-positive and negative groups.

pmc-13597881.title: Infarct volume versus NIHSS score for ischemic and bleeding risk stratification after acute ischemic stroke
pmc-13597881.creator: Zi-Mo Chen, Ying-Yu Jiang, Hong-Qiu Gu, Xin-Miao Zhang, Jing Jing, Jing-Lin Mo, Yong Jiang, Li-Ping Liu, Xing-Quan Zhao, Yong-Jun Wang, Zi-Xiao Li
pmc-13597881.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundWhether infarct volume refines assessment of recurrent ischemic stroke (IS) and intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) risk following acute IS beyond the National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) remains uncertain. We compared their performance in ischemic-hemorrhagic risk stratification.MethodsWe included 10,545 patients with acute IS from the Third China National Stroke Registry (CNSR-III) with diffusion-weighted imaging/apparent diffusion coefficient-derived infarct volume and NIHSS data. Outcomes were 90-day recurrent IS and ICH, analyzed separately.

uslaw-usc-t16-s715h.title: 16 U.S.C. § 715h — Operation of State game laws
uslaw-usc-t16-s715h.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t16-s715h.description: United States Code, Title 16 (Conservation); Chapter 7 (Protection Of Migratory Game And Insectivorous Birds); Subchapter III (Migratory Bird Conservation). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. Nothing in this subchapter is intended to interfere with the operation of the game laws of the several States applying to migratory game birds insofar as they do not permit what is forbidden by Federal law.
